extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (computational algebraists / developers using SINGULAR libraries gitfan.lib, GND.lib, gradedModules.lib)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation of procedures in SINGULAR libraries (gitfan.lib, GND.lib, gradedModules.lib): usage lines, purposes, return values, assumptions and examples for each procedure so users can call and interpret them correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: storeActionOnOrbitConeIndices
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: Write the action on the set of orbit cones to the file fn in Singular readable format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: storeActionOnOrbitConeIndices(generatorsGperm,st); arguments: string generatorsGperm:list, fn:string. Return: nothing. (Procedure from library gitfan.lib; see Section D.15.16.)

rubrics_metrics.name: permutationFromIntvec
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: Create a permutation from an intvec of images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: permutationFromIntvec(sigmaImage); sigmaImage: intvec. Return: permutation. Example: permutation sigma = permutationFromIntvec(intvec( 1, 2, 4, 3, 5, 7, 6, 9, 8, 10 )); sigma; shows permutation output.

rubrics_metrics.name: permutationToIntvec
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: Convert a permutation to an intvec of images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: permutationToIntvec(sigma); sigma: permutation. Return: intvec. Example: permutationToIntvec(sigma); yields '1,2,4,3,5,7,6,9,8,10'. (Procedure from gitfan.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: evaluateProduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: Evaluates a formal product of variables xi in st, where xi corresponds to the permutation generatorsGperm[i].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: evaluateProduct(generatorsGperm,st); generatorsGperm: list, st: string. Return: permutation. Example code shows building generators, computing group actions and an elementInTermsOfGenerators string representing a product; evaluateProduct would evaluate such an element (example call commented out in the doc).

rubrics_metrics.name: GITfanSymmetric
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: Returns the common refinement of the cones given in the list OC which is supposed to contain the orbit cones intersected with Qgamma. The list actiononorbitcones is supposed to contain the symmetry group acting as permutations on the list of orbit cones in OC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: GITfanSymmetric(OC, Q, Qgamma, actiononorbitcones [, file1, file2]); OC:list, Q:bigintmat, Qgamma:cone, actiononorbitcones: list of intvec, file1:string, file2:string. The optional file arguments: first file will contain hashes of the GIT-cones; second file (if given) will contain the actual cones in H-representation. To obtain the whole GIT-fan Qgamma has to be the cone generated by the columns of Q. Return: a list containing the bigint hashes of the GIT cones. Example provided with step-by-step construction of AF, OC, symmetry group, and call; printed debug/time output shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: GITfanParallelSymmetric
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: Returns the common refinement of the cones given in the list OC which is supposed to contain the orbit cones intersected with Qgamma. The list actiononorbitcones is supposed to contain the symmetry group acting as permutations on the list of orbit cones in OC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: GITfanParallelSymmetric(OC, Q, Qgamma, actiononorbitcones [, file1]); OC:list, Q:bigintmat, Qgamma:cone, actiononorbitcones: list of intvec, file1:string. Return: a list containing the bigint hashes of the GIT cones. Note: The procedure uses parallel computation for construction of the GIT-cones. Example illustrates building inputs and calling GITfanParallelSymmetric; output is list of hashes and timing/log messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: bigintToBinary
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: Convert a bigint n (assumed < 2^r) to an intvec with entries the positions of 1 in the r-bit binary representation of n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: bigintToBinary(n, r): n bigint, r int. Assume n is smaller than 2^r. Return: an intvec, with entries the positions of 1 in the binary representation of n with r bits. Example: bigintToBinary(bigint(2)^90-1, 90); returns 1,2,...,90.

rubrics_metrics.name: applyPermutationToIntvec
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: Apply permutation g to the set of entries of intvec v and return a sorted intvec of the images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: applyPermutationToIntvec(v,g); v: intvec, g: permutation. The result is a sorted intvec. Assume the entries of v are valid arguments of g; input need not be sorted. Return: intvec. Example: applyPermutationToIntvec(intvec(1, 3, 4, 6, 8), g); yields 4,5,6,7,10 for given g.

rubrics_metrics.name: hashToCone
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: Given a bigint hash v and a list OC of orbit cones (used in hash representation of GIT cones), returns the cone that is the intersection of the cones in OC according to the binary representation of the hash v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: hashToCone(v, OC): v bigint, OC list of cones. The elements of OC are the orbit cones used in the hash representation of the GIT cones. Return: a cone (the intersection). Example shows constructing AF, OC, setting v=21300544 and calling hashToCone(v, OC) producing AMBIENT_DIM, FACETS, LINEAR_SPAN output.

rubrics_metrics.name: hashesToFan
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: Given a list of bigint hashes and the corresponding list OC of orbit cones, constructs a fan whose maximal cones are the intersections of cones in OC according to the binary representations of the hashes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: hashesToFan(hashes, OC): hashes list of bigint, OC list of cones. The elements of OC are the orbit cones used in the hash representation of the GIT cones. Return: a fan. Example shows building OC and calling GITfanParallel and then fan Sigma = hashesToFan(GIT,OC).

rubrics_metrics.name: gitCone
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: Returns the GIT-cone lambda(w), i.e. the intersection of all orbit cones containing the vector w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: gitCone(a, Q, w); a: ideal, Q:bigintmat, w:bigintmat. Note: call this only if you are interested in a single GIT-cone. Return: a cone. Example: given Q and w, gitCone returns lambda with rays(...) output.

rubrics_metrics.name: desingularization
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: Returns as output a General Neron Desingularization as in the referenced paper (A. Popescu, D. Popescu, arXiv:1508.05511).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: desingularization(All, nra,nrx,nry,xid,yid,aid,f[, "debug"]); (Procedure from library GND.lib). The procedure computes a General Neron Desingularization in the frame of one-dimensional local domains. Return: printed/described output (list h, kernel, minors, matrices, etc.). Example calls demonstrate inputs (rings, ideals, polynomials) and show verbose debug output when "debug" argument is provided. The doc prints intermediate data like ker, minors, vidjet, h, G, QT, f, g.

rubrics_metrics.name: grobj
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: create a valid graded object with a given matrix presentation, weighting and optional total graded degrees (for columns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: grobj(M, w[, d]), where M is matrix/ideal/module, intvec w is row weighting, optional d are total graded degrees. Return: graded object with matrix presentation M, row weighting w [and total graded degrees d of columns]. Notes: If M has zero columns it should have attrib(M,'degHomog') set. Examples show constructing grobj for various modules and inspecting grview output; zero object examples included.

rubrics_metrics.name: grtest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: grtest(M[,b]), anything M, optionally int b. Return: 1 if M is a valid graded object, 0 otherwise. If b is not given print an invalid object message. M should be an ideal or module or matrix, with weighting attribute 'isHomog' and optionally 'degHomog'. Attributes must be compatible with presentation matrix. Examples show calls that fail and valid calls with commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: grdeg
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: graded degrees of columns (generators) of M, describing the source of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: grdeg(M), for graded object M. Return: intvec of degrees. Assume: M must be a graded object (matrix/module/ideal/mapping). Note: if M has zero cols it should have attrib(M,'degHomog') set. Examples illustrate use with grobj-created modules and composition operations; returns degree vectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: grview
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: print the degree/grading data about the graded matrix/module/ideal/mapping object M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage: grview(M), graded object M. Return: nothing (prints information). Assume: M must be graded. Examples show formatted output describing graded homomorphism, source/target degrees, and other metadata for various constructed graded objects.
